finding.text: The owner's on-screen "undefined" came from the chat view, and the view is still not fixed. `public/framework/ext/Chat/v3/ChatV3.js:156` draws every non-Prompt root as `first_words(m.text)`, and `ChatV3.js:221` does `String(text ?? "")`. Before this change a generic `Item` had no `.text`, so the screen showed "undefined". After it, a `{icon, title}` card draws as an empty, untitled note: `m.title` and `m.icon` are never drawn, and neither is `content`. `ChatList.js:65` draws a title only for a Prompt. So "the owner asked for a card and it must work" is not met on the owner's screen. Fix `note()` (and ChatList's note) to draw `icon` + `title` + `content`, and test that a card shows its title.

Any other unregistered type an agent guesses (e.g. `type:"Note"`, `"Task card"`) still becomes a generic Item, and `ChatV3.note` still renders the word "undefined" for it. The alias at `Message.js` (`Message.TYPES.Card = Message`) covers only one guess. The cause is the view's `m.text` on a member that has no `text` getter. Guard it in the view, or make Chat hydrate an unknown type as a Message.

"or a ref to an existing item" (requirements ask 3, the owner's first bullet) is not addressed anywhere: no call is named, there is no test, and neither the readme nor the brief lines mention it. `content` is a plain `List`, so `content:{add:{type:"Ref", ...}}` probably works, but it is unproven and undocumented.

The upgrade path is invisible in the main view. `ChatV3.js:60` never draws a Reply as a root, and `reply()` at `ChatV3.js:192` ignores `title`/`icon`. So "upgrading" a Reply into a card by setting its title (the readme's claim, `core/Session/Chat/readme.md` card bullet) changes nothing the owner sees. The test (`Servex/agents/card-messages.test.mjs`, step 3) only proves the data changed.

`risk.md`'s Decision says the three brief lines are "one example call, one line on upgrading an existing message, one line saying type is never needed". The lines actually added to `Servex/agents/single-voice-assistant.md:25-26` are a card example (which also says no type) and an append line. There is no upgrade line, so the record and the change disagree.

The brief line says "never a `type`", while the readme and the code alias `type:"Card"` on purpose. Both are true, but a fresh agent reading only one of them gets mixed signals. One sentence in the readme ("the alias is a safety net; write no type") would settle it.

The test writes its scratch sessions into the live store (`public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/16/.card-messages-test-*`). The dev server watches that tree, and a crash between `mkdir` and `finally` leaves a stray folder there. An OS temp dir would be safer, if `run_item` accepts one.

There is no task.jsonl in the minion folder (only `session.jsonl` with the finish line), and `requirements.md` lives in the parent's `ask3-cards-by-id/` folder. A fresh agent can continue from that folder only if it knows to look there. The finish line does name the commit, `cacdb7e07` on `worktree/qf-5`, which is not yet merged.
Verified: in the qf-5 worktree, `card-messages.test.mjs` passes 10/10, `chat-messages.test.mjs` 22/22 and `Chat.test.mjs` 26/26. The `page_tools.js` read-back change (`?? ""`) is correct and small.

The Chat v3 readme is out of date. `ext/Chat/v3/readme.md:10` still says a plain Message is "its own small card", with no word about a card's icon, title and content, or an upgraded Reply drawing as a card. Lines 36–37 still give `placement.test.mjs` as 18 checks (it is 24 now) and `ChatV3.test.mjs` as 16 checks, and don't list the new card checks (CLAUDE.md law 9).

`Message.js:9-10` (the comment on `TYPES`) still says "A name not here falls back to Item.hydrate's rule". After this diff that is false: only `"Ref"` gets through, and every other name builds a Message (`Message.js:188-190`). A fresh agent who reads only that comment will get it wrong.

`risk.md` and `requirements.md` in `session-e9c8d0d3/mastermind-voice-system/ask3-cards-by-id/` are untracked in the main checkout (`git status` shows `??`). The brief asked for `risk.md` as a deliverable. Committed state is the only record, so one cleanup deletes the brief and the risk record. Commit them, or move them into the worktree branch.

`Message.hydrate` now falls back to `Message`, not `this` (`Message.js:190`). An untyped `Prompt.hydrate({...})` or `Reply.hydrate({...})` would build a plain Message. Nothing calls those today (grep), and the real store only ever wrote Prompt/Reply/Ref/Message types (88 Ref, 212 Prompt, 190 Reply, 3 Message), so nothing breaks yet. Still, `Known ?? this` would keep the old subclass behaviour at no cost.

`ChatList.js:286-293` draws card content again in its own way, instead of calling `note_view` (`placement.js:433`). It also skips `label()`, so a `{type:"Ref"}` content line draws as an empty row in the list view. In Chat v3 the same line shows the Ref's label. One `note_view` call would fix both (Law 6).

`ChatList.js` adds `chatlist-icon`, `chatlist-content` and `chatlist-content-line`, but `ChatList.css` has no rules for them. Content lines get no indent or rule like v3's `.chat-v3-content-line`, and the icon sits on its own line.

Every finding from the first review is fixed. The view draws icon, title and content (`ChatV3.js:365-375`). Any unknown type now builds a Message. A Ref in a card's content works end to end (test step 4). An upgraded Reply draws as a card (`ChatV3.js:384-392`). The `risk.md` Decision now matches the three brief lines (`single-voice-assistant.md:153-155`). I could not re-run `ChatV3.test.mjs` without a dev server for the worktree. The minion's log says it passed against 127.0.0.1:65495.
Verified in worktree qf-5 at 677cc23d2: `card-messages` 14/14, `placement` 24/24, `chat-messages` 22/22, `Chat.test` 26/26. Both commits are still unmerged on `worktree/qf-5`, as the brief asked.

The list view never redraws when content is added to a card. `public/framework/ext/Chat/list/ChatList.js:26` marks a bubble dirty only when the `delta` event's `from` is a Message. For `{messages:{"<id>":{content:{add:…}}}}`, `from` is the card's `content` List (checked with `Session.replay` + `on("delta")` in qf-5). So the appended line shows only after a reload. Chat v3 handles this with `card_for()`'s `.parent` check (`ChatV3.js:371`); ChatList needs the same walk up to the owning Message.

The ChatList readme is out of date. `public/framework/ext/Chat/list/readme.md` doesn't say the view now draws a card's icon, title and content lines, or that it imports `note_view` from `../v3/placement.js`, a link between the two modules. CLAUDE.md law 9 asks the readme to state this.

"Read it by that id" works only partly through `item({path})`. `Servex/agents/page_tools.js:139` returns a card's `content` as a count, not its lines, and only the last 20 messages. An agent can't read back what it appended, and can't read an older card at all. A line in the seat brief, or an answer that includes the content lines, would close this.

Code comments point at review rounds a later reader will never see, such as "review finding 1/4" (`ChatV3.js:200`, `placement.js:446`) and "review note 7" (`card-messages.test.mjs:26`). They should say what the code does and why, without the history.
The two earlier reviews' fixes are in, checked in worktree qf-5:
Recorded sessions use only the message types Message, Prompt, Ref and Reply (grep of every `session.jsonl`). So the stricter `Message.hydrate` doesn't change how any existing line loads.

`public/framework/core/Session/readme.md:120` ("What item() answers for a session") has no row for `messages`. It should say what `item()` returns: `count`, and the last 20 from `message_view`, each `{id, type, by, at, text, title?, icon?, content?}`. It also never mentions the new by-id read, `{messages:{"<id>":{}}}`, which `walk_queries` answers (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:1037`). `page_tools.js` points readers at this section, so a fresh agent can't learn from it how to read a card back (CLAUDE.md law 9).

The header of `Servex/agents/card-messages.test.mjs:41-43` says `run_item` "cannot address a folder outside the repo at all — there is no 'accept a temp dir' form". That is false: `page_tools.js:17` reads `SERVEX_PUBLIC` for exactly this, and `ref-cache.test.mjs` uses it. Because of that belief, the test writes its scratch sessions into the real store (`ai/sessions/2026/10/16/.card-messages-test-*`), so a killed run leaves junk there and the file watchers see it. Point `SERVEX_PUBLIC` at an OS temp tree, and fix the comment.

The round-3 log says the review-history comments were stripped, but some are still there: `ChatV3.test.mjs:83` ("review finding 1/4"), `placement.test.mjs:50,59,62,66` ("review finding 1/2", "2/3", "finding 2", "finding 4"), `ChatList.test.mjs:25,34` ("finding 1") and `card-messages.test.mjs:42` ("review note 7"). A later reader can't see those reviews.

`ChatList.test.mjs` copies its fixture to `fixture/live-list-<pid>.jsonl` before the `try` (line 14), so if `get_browser()` fails, the copy is left behind. The path is also not gitignored: `.gitignore:237` covers only `ext/Chat/v3/fixture/live-*.jsonl`.

`ChatList.test.mjs:29` waits for `.chatlist-title`, a class that doesn't exist, and swallows the timeout with `.catch(()=>{})`. That adds up to 8 s of dead wait per run. The next line's `waitForFunction` already does the real check.

`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:13` now imports a view-side module, `public/framework/ext/Chat/v3/placement.js`, for `note_view`. That is fine while `placement.js` stays DOM-free, but the only place this is recorded is a code comment. One line in `placement.js`'s header or the v3 readme ("Servex's item tool imports note_view; keep it node-safe") would protect it.
